Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-DF42BEB029-97975
Member: Quinn Ellison, Member ID W391580594
Requested service: Partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement, CPT 27446
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-04
Treating surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (unicompartmental knee arthroplasty) dated 2026-08-04. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree and ask that this determination be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below.

I understand that Aetna evaluates requests for knee arthroplasty, including unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, under Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html). I was not provided the specific version or effective date of the policy applied to my case, so I am requesting that Aetna confirm [the exact version/effective date of CPB 0660 used in this review] and identify any policy criteria relied upon that are not addressed below.

The publicly posted version of CPB 0660 that I reviewed states that unicompartmental knee arthroplasty "is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria," including:

"Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination; and Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament; and Patient's knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less; and Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) ... affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint; and History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record ... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)."

The policy further states that qualifying conservative therapy "includes all of the following, unless contraindicated: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and Activity modification; and Supervised physical therapy (activities of daily living [ADLs] diminished despite completing a plan of care); and Assistive device use ... and Therapeutic injections into the knee."

Applying these criteria to my clinical record:

1. Radiographic/imaging evidence of single-compartment, advanced osteoarthritis. My MRI of 2026-05-28 documented "full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition" and "Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially." This is direct radiographic evidence of Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 disease confined to a single (medial) compartment, which is the specific imaging finding the policy language above identifies as satisfying the radiographic criterion. I believe this directly contradicts the denial rationale that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure," and I ask that the reviewer re-examine the 2026-05-28 MRI report against this criterion.

2. Pain and functional disability interfering with activities of daily living. I have had 18 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3-4 times nightly due to pain. This documents ongoing functional disability and pain interfering with ADLs.

3. Physical examination findings. My exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, consistent with the policy's exam-based criterion of "limited range of motion" on physical examination. [The record excerpt provided does not separately document effusion/swelling or crepitus; if needed, the surgeon can supply an addendum addressing this element.]

4. History of unsuccessful conservative therapy, including formal physical therapy. I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17, 24 visits) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This falls within the policy's stated 12-24 week window and consists of formal, in-person, supervised physical therapy — satisfying the requirement that "at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consist[] of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)."

5. Anti-inflammatory/analgesic medication trial. I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, addressing the "anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics" element of conservative therapy.

6. Therapeutic injection. I received a corticosteroid injection into the knee on 2026-05-02, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief, addressing the "therapeutic injections into the knee" element of conservative therapy. [If surgery is scheduled within 12 weeks of this injection date, please note that CPB 0660 also lists "corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty" as an absolute contraindication to joint replacement; the surgeon will confirm the planned surgical date is [outside/inside] that 12-week window, currently listed here as [surgical date not provided in the record excerpt].]

7. Absence of documented contraindications. The record excerpt provided does not report any active joint infection, active skin infection at the surgical site, uncontrolled systemic bacteremia, vascular insufficiency, significant muscular atrophy, neuromuscular disease, inadequate bone stock, or implant-component allergy — the absolute contraindications identified in CPB 0660. It also does not report prior proximal tibial or distal femoral osteotomy, tibial/femoral shaft deformity, radiographic subluxation, flexion contracture greater than 15 degrees, varus/valgus deformity beyond the thresholds stated in the policy, inflammatory or crystalline arthropathy, or subchondral cysts/osteonecrosis — the relative contraindications specific to unicompartmental knee arthroplasty under CPB 0660. [If Aetna's review identified any of these findings in the submitted file, please specify which finding and where it is documented so it can be addressed directly; the surgeon can also submit an addendum specifically attesting to ligament stability, including an intact anterior cruciate ligament, and to the measured knee arc of motion, if this documentation was not already part of the submitted packet.]

8. Additional relevant history. I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29 (below the policy's morbid-obesity relative-contraindication threshold of BMI greater than 40), and I am a non-smoker. [If applicable, diabetic HbA1c status was not addressed in the record excerpt provided; if I am diabetic, my surgeon will confirm HbA1c is below 8% within 3 months prior to surgery as referenced in the policy's additional note.]

For these reasons, I believe the clinical record — including the 2026-05-28 MRI showing Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4, single-compartment (medial), bone-on-bone disease, together with 16 weeks of documented supervised physical therapy, an 8-month NSAID trial, and a corticosteroid injection with only transient benefit — meets the medical-necessity criteria for unicompartmental knee arthroplasty as stated in CPB 0660, and directly contradicts the stated denial reason that the imaging findings do not support medical necessity.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice, which specifies that my appeal must be received by 2027-01-31.

Please find enclosed/attached:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17)
- MRI report dated 2026-05-28
- Office visit/exam notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-02)
- [Letter of medical necessity/addendum from Dr. Lindqvist, if available]

I request a full review of this appeal, including reconsideration by a physician reviewer with appropriate orthopedic expertise, and a written determination consistent with the timeframes required for my plan. If any additional information is needed, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or my surgeon's office at [surgeon's office phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Quinn Ellison
Member ID: W391580594
[Phone number]
[Email address]

Enclosures: as listed above

Note: All text in quotation marks above is quoted directly from the publicly posted Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html). All other statements are my own summary or argument and are not quotations from Aetna.
